title.zh: 卷一百九十八 列傳第八十五: 孝友二
title.en: Volume 198 Biographies 85: Filial and Brotherly Acts 1
title.raw: 卷一百九十八 列傳第八十五: 孝友二 Volume 198 Biographies 85: Filial and Brotherly Acts 1

sentences.zh: 王庸，字伯常，雄州歸信人。

translations.literal: Wang Yong, style name Bochang, was a native of Guixin in Xiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yong, whose style was Bochang, came from Guixin in Xiong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 事母李氏以孝聞。

translations.literal: In serving his mother, Lady Li, he became renowned for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He won fame for filial devotion in caring for his mother, Lady Li.

sentences.zh: 母有疾，庸夜禱北辰，至叩頭出血，母疾遂愈。

translations.literal: When his mother fell ill, Yong prayed by night to the North Star, until his forehead bled from knocking it on the ground; his mother's illness then recovered.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell ill, Yong spent the nights praying to the Pole Star, bowing until his forehead bled; her illness then lifted.

sentences.zh: 及母卒，哀毀幾絕，露處墓前，旦夕悲號。

translations.literal: When his mother died, his grief and emaciation nearly killed him; he dwelt in the open before the grave, wailing morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: After her death his mourning was so severe he nearly perished, living unsheltered at the grave and lamenting from dawn till dusk.

sentences.zh: 一夕，雷雨暴至，鄰人持寢席往，欲蔽之，見庸所坐臥之地獨不沾濕，咸嘆異而去。

translations.literal: One night a violent thunderstorm burst upon him; neighbors brought bedding to shelter him, but saw that the ground where Yong sat and lay alone was not wet; all marveled and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: One night a thunderstorm broke over him; neighbors brought bedding to cover him, yet the spot where Yong sat and slept alone stayed dry—everyone marveled and went away.

sentences.zh: 復有蜜蜂數十房，來止其家，歲得蜜蠟，以供祭祀。

translations.literal: Moreover, several dozen hives of bees came to lodge at his home; each year he obtained honey and wax to supply sacrificial offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of beehives also settled at his home, yielding honey and wax each year for his ancestral rites.

sentences.zh: 黃贇，字止敬，臨江人。

translations.literal: Huang Yin, style name Zhijing, was a native of Linjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Yin, styled Zhijing, was from Linjiang.

sentences.zh: 父君道，延祐間求官京師，留贇江南。

translations.literal: His father Jundao, during the Yanyou era, sought office in the capital and left Yin in the south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jundao went to the capital during the Yanyou reign to seek office, leaving Yin behind in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 時贇年幼，及既長，聞其父娶後妻居永平，乃往省之，則父歿已三年矣。

translations.literal: At the time Yin was young; when he had grown up, he heard that his father had taken a second wife and lived in Yongping, and went to visit him—only to find his father had been dead three years.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was still a child then; when he grew up he learned his father had remarried and lived in Yongping, and set out to see him—only to find his father had died three years before.

sentences.zh: 庶母聞贇來，盡挾其貲去，更嫁，拒不見贇。

translations.literal: When his stepmother heard Yin was coming, she took all the property and left, remarried, and refused to see Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing he was coming, his stepmother seized everything of value, remarried elsewhere, and refused to meet him.

sentences.zh: 贇號哭語人曰：「吾之來，為省吾父也。

translations.literal: Yin wailed and said to people: "I came to visit my father.
translations.idiomatic: Yin wept aloud and told others, "I came only to see my father.

sentences.zh: 今不幸吾父已歿，思奉其柩歸而窆之，莫知其墓。

translations.literal: Now, alas, my father is already dead; I wish to bring his coffin home and bury it, but I do not know where his grave is.
translations.idiomatic: Now he is gone, and I long to bring his coffin home for burial, yet I do not know where he lies.

sentences.zh: 苟得見庶母示以葬所，死不恨矣，尚忍利遺財邪！」

translations.literal: If only I could see my stepmother and have her show me the burial place, I would die without regret—how could I still covet leftover wealth!"
translations.idiomatic: If my stepmother would only show me the grave, I would die content—how could I still care about any money she left behind!"

sentences.zh: 久之，聞庶母居海濱，亟裹糧往。

translations.literal: After a long while he heard his stepmother lived by the seashore; he quickly packed provisions and went.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually he heard she was living on the coast; he packed food at once and set out.

sentences.zh: 庶母复拒之，三日不納。

translations.literal: His stepmother again refused him and for three days would not admit him.
translations.idiomatic: She turned him away again and would not let him in for three days.

sentences.zh: 庶母之弟憐之，與偕至永平屬縣樂亭求父墓，又弗得。

translations.literal: His stepmother's younger brother pitied him and went with him to Leting, a county subordinate to Yongping, to seek his father's grave, but again they did not find it.
translations.idiomatic: Her younger brother took pity on him and went with him to Leting in Yongping to search for the grave, but they still could not find it.

sentences.zh: 贇哭禱於神，一夕夢老父以杖指葬處曰：「見片磚即可得。

translations.literal: Yin wept and prayed to the spirits; one night he dreamed his aged father pointed with a staff to the burial place and said: "When you see a broken brick you will find it.
translations.idiomatic: Yin wept and prayed to the gods; one night he dreamed his father pointed with a staff to the burial spot and said, "You will find it where you see a broken brick.

sentences.zh: 明日就其地求之，庶母之弟曰：「真是已，斂時有某物可驗。」

translations.literal: " The next day he searched there; his stepmother's younger brother said: "This is truly it—when he was interred there was a certain object that can verify it."
translations.idiomatic: " The next day he searched there; her brother said, "This is the place—there was a certain object placed in the coffin when he was buried that will prove it."

sentences.zh: 啟朽棺，得父骨以歸。

translations.literal: They opened the decayed coffin, obtained their father's bones, and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: They opened the rotted coffin, recovered his father's remains, and carried them home.

sentences.zh: 石明三者，與母居餘姚山中。

translations.literal: Shi Mingsan lived with his mother in the mountains of Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Mingsan and his mother lived in the mountains of Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 一日明三自外歸，覓母不見，見壁穿而臥內有三虎子，知母為虎所害。

translations.literal: One day Mingsan returned from outside, sought his mother and did not see her; he saw a hole in the wall and within the den three tiger cubs—he knew his mother had been killed by a tiger.
translations.idiomatic: One day Mingsan came home from outside and could not find his mother; a hole had been torn in the wall, and inside the den lay three tiger cubs—he knew a tiger had killed her.

sentences.zh: 乃盡殺虎子，礪巨斧立壁側，伺母虎至，斫其腦裂而死。

translations.literal: He then killed all the cubs, sharpened a great axe and stood by the wall, waited for the mother tiger to come, and split her skull so that she died.
translations.idiomatic: He killed every cub, sharpened a great axe, and waited by the wall; when the mother tiger came he split her skull and killed her.

sentences.zh: 復往倚岩石傍，執斧伺候，斫殺牡虎。

translations.literal: He then went to lean against a rock, holding the axe in wait, and struck and killed the male tiger.
translations.idiomatic: He went next to a boulder, axe in hand, and when the male tiger appeared he struck and killed it too.

sentences.zh: 明三亦立死不僕，張目如生，所執斧牢不可拔。

translations.literal: Mingsan also stood dead without falling; his eyes were open as in life, and the axe he held could not be pulled free.
translations.idiomatic: Mingsan too stood dead without falling, eyes wide as though alive, and the axe in his grip could not be wrested away.

sentences.zh: 劉琦，岳州臨湘人。

translations.literal: Liu Qi was a native of Linxiang in Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qi came from Linxiang in Yue Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 生二歲而母劉氏遭亂陷於兵，琦獨事其父。

translations.literal: When he was two years old his mother, the Lady Liu, was lost in the turmoil of war; Qi alone served his father.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of two his mother, Lady Liu, was taken captive in the wars; Qi grew up serving only his father.

sentences.zh: 稍長，思其母不置，常歎曰：「人皆有母，而我獨無！」

translations.literal: When he grew somewhat older, he could not put his mother from his mind and often sighed: "Every person has a mother, yet I alone have none!"
translations.idiomatic: As he grew he could not stop thinking of her and would sigh, "Everyone has a mother—why must I alone have none!"

sentences.zh: 輒歔欷泣下。

translations.literal: He would then sob and weep.
translations.idiomatic: He would then burst into tears.

sentences.zh: 及冠，請於父，往求其母。

translations.literal: When he came of age, he asked his father's leave and went to seek his mother.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he begged his father's permission and set out to find her.

sentences.zh: 遍歷河之南北、淮之東西，數歲不得。

translations.literal: He traveled throughout north and south of the Yellow River and east and west of the Huai, and for several years did not find her.
translations.idiomatic: For years he searched north and south of the Yellow River and east and west of the Huai, without success.

sentences.zh: 後求得於池州之貴池，迎以歸養。

translations.literal: Later he found her at Guichi in Chizhou and brought her home to support her.
translations.idiomatic: He finally found her at Guichi in Chizhou and brought her home to care for her.

sentences.zh: 其後十五年而父歿，又三年而母歿，終喪猶蔬食。

translations.literal: Fifteen years later his father died; three years after that his mother died, and even after the mourning period ended he still ate only vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen years later his father died; three years after that his mother died, and he continued to eat only plain food even after mourning ended.

sentences.zh: 有司上其事，旌表其門曰「孝義」。

translations.literal: The authorities reported the matter upward and honored his gate with the inscription "Filial Righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: Officials reported his conduct to the court, and his gate was honored with the plaque "Filial Righteousness."

sentences.zh: 劉源，歸德中牟人。

translations.literal: Liu Yuan was a native of Zhongmou in Guide.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan came from Zhongmou in Guide Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 母吳氏，年七十餘，病甚不能行。

translations.literal: His mother, the Lady Wu, was over seventy years old, gravely ill and unable to walk.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Wu, was over seventy, gravely ill and unable to walk.

sentences.zh: 適兵火起，且延至其家，鄰里俱逃，源力不能救，乃呼天號泣，趨入抱母，為火所焚而死。

translations.literal: Just then war-fires broke out and soon reached his home; the neighbors all fled. Yuan had not the strength to save her, so he cried to Heaven and wept aloud, rushed in and embraced his mother, and was burned to death by the fire.
translations.idiomatic: War-fires broke out and soon reached his home; neighbors fled, and Yuan, powerless to save her, cried to Heaven, rushed in to embrace his mother, and perished in the flames with her.

sentences.zh: 祝公榮，字大昌，處州麗水人。

translations.literal: Zhu Gongrong, style name Dachang, was a native of Lishui in Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Gongrong, styled Dachang, was from Lishui in Chu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 隱居養親，事母甚孝。

translations.literal: He lived in seclusion to support his parents and served his mother with great filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement to care for his parents and was deeply filial toward his mother.

sentences.zh: 母歿，居喪盡禮。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he observed mourning in full accordance with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he observed every detail of mourning ritual.

sentences.zh: 灶突失火，公榮力不能救，乃伏棺悲哭，其火自滅，鄉里異之。

translations.literal: The kitchen chimney caught fire; Gongrong had not the strength to save it, so he lay upon the coffin and wept in grief—the fire extinguished itself, and the village marveled.
translations.idiomatic: A kitchen fire broke out; powerless to fight it, Gongrong lay weeping on his mother's coffin—and the fire went out by itself, to the wonder of the whole village.

sentences.zh: 塑二親像於堂，朝夕事之如事生焉。

translations.literal: He molded images of both parents in the hall and morning and evening served them as though they were living.
translations.idiomatic: He had statues of both parents made for the hall and tended them morning and evening as if they were still alive.

sentences.zh: 陸思孝，紹興山陰樵者，性至孝。

translations.literal: Lu Sixiao was a woodcutter of Shanyin in Shaoxing, whose nature was utmost filial.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Sixiao, a woodcutter from Shanyin in Shaoxing, was profoundly filial by nature.

sentences.zh: 母老病痢，思孝醫禱久之，不效。

translations.literal: His aged mother suffered from dysentery; Sixiao sought physicians and prayed for a long time, without effect.
translations.idiomatic: His elderly mother suffered from dysentery; Sixiao sought doctors and prayed for a long time, all to no avail.

sentences.zh: 思孝方欲刲股肉為糜以進，忽夢寐間怳若有神人者授以藥劑，思孝得而異之，即以奉母，其疾遂愈。

translations.literal: Sixiao was just about to cut flesh from his thigh to make gruel for her when suddenly in sleep it seemed a divine being gave him a medicine; Sixiao received it in wonder and at once offered it to his mother, and her illness then recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Sixiao was about to cut flesh from his thigh to make gruel for her when, in a dream, a spirit seemed to hand him a medicine; he gave it to his mother at once, and she recovered.

sentences.zh: 姜兼，嚴州淳安人。

translations.literal: Jiang Jian was a native of Chun'an in Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Jian came from Chun'an in Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 七歲而孤，與二兄養母至孝。

translations.literal: Orphaned at seven, he and his two elder brothers supported their mother with utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at seven, he and his two elder brothers cared for their mother with devoted filial piety.

sentences.zh: 母死，兼哀慕幾絕。

translations.literal: When his mother died, Jian's grief and longing nearly killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, Jian's grief nearly destroyed him.

sentences.zh: 既葬，獨居墓下，朝夕哭奠，寂焉荒山中，躬自樵爨，蔬食飲水，一衰麻寒暑不易。

translations.literal: After the burial he dwelt alone beneath the grave, weeping and offering sacrifices morning and evening in the silent wild mountains; he himself gathered firewood and cooked, ate vegetables and drank water, and wore the same hemp mourning garb through cold and heat without change.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial he lived alone at the grave, mourning morning and evening in the lonely mountains; he cut his own firewood, cooked his own food, ate only vegetables and drank only water, and wore the same hemp mourning clothes through winter and summer alike.

sentences.zh: 同里陳氏、戴氏子不能事其父母，聞兼之行，慚感而悔，皆迎養焉。

translations.literal: Sons of the Chen and Dai families in the same village who could not serve their parents, hearing of Jian's conduct, were ashamed, moved, and repented, and all brought their parents home to support them.
translations.idiomatic: Young men of the Chen and Dai families nearby who had neglected their parents, hearing of Jian's example, were shamed into repentance and brought their parents home to care for them.

sentences.zh: 胡伴侶，鈞州密縣人。

translations.literal: Hu Banlü was a native of Mi County in Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Banlü came from Mi County in Jun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其父實嘗患心疾數月，幾死，更數醫俱莫能療。

translations.literal: His father Shi once suffered from heart disease for several months and nearly died; several physicians in succession could not cure him.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shi suffered a heart ailment for months and nearly died; physician after physician failed to cure him.

sentences.zh: 伴侶乃齋沐焚香，泣告於天，以所佩小刀於右脅傍刲其皮膚，割脂一片，煎藥以進，父疾遂瘳，其傷亦旋愈。

translations.literal: Banlü then purified himself with fasting and bathing, burned incense, and weeping reported to Heaven; with the small knife he wore he cut the skin beside his right ribs, sliced off a piece of fat, boiled it into medicine and presented it—his father's illness then recovered, and his wound also soon healed.
translations.idiomatic: Banlü fasted, bathed, burned incense, and wept his plea to Heaven; with the knife at his belt he cut the flesh beside his right ribs, took a slice of fat, boiled it into medicine for his father—and Shi recovered, while Banlü's wound healed as well.

sentences.zh: 朝廷旌表其門。

translations.literal: The court honored his gate.
translations.idiomatic: The court honored his household with an official commendation.

sentences.zh: 王士弘，延安中部人。

translations.literal: Wang Shihong was a native of Zhongbu in Yan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shihong came from Zhongbu in Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 父摶有疾，士弘傾家貲求醫，見醫即拜，遍禱諸神，叩額成瘡。

translations.literal: His father Tuan fell ill; Shihong exhausted the family wealth seeking physicians, bowed to every doctor he met, prayed to all the gods, and knocked his forehead until sores formed.
translations.idiomatic: When his father Tuan fell ill, Shihong spent the family fortune on doctors, bowed to every physician he met, prayed to every god he knew, and battered his forehead until it bled and festered.

sentences.zh: 父歿，哀毀盡禮，廬墓三年，足未嘗至家。

translations.literal: When his father died, his grief and emaciation fulfilled every ritual requirement; he built a hut by the grave for three years and his feet never once reached home.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he mourned with scrupulous ritual, dwelling in a hut by the grave for three years without once setting foot in his house.

sentences.zh: 墓廬上有奇鵲來巢，飛鳥翔集，與士弘親近，若相狎然，眾咸異之。

translations.literal: On the grave hut a rare magpie came to nest; flying birds gathered and were intimate with Shihong, as if playing together—all marveled.
translations.idiomatic: A rare magpie nested on his mourning hut; birds gathered there and grew tame with Shihong, as though at play—to everyone's wonder.

sentences.zh: 終喪，復建祠於塋前，朔望必往奠祭，雖風雨不廢也。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he again built a shrine before the tomb mound and on the first and fifteenth of each month always went to offer sacrifice, never omitting this even in wind and rain.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he built a shrine at the grave and never missed the new- and full-moon offerings, rain or shine.

sentences.zh: 有司上其事於朝，旌表之。

translations.literal: The authorities reported the matter to the court and honored him.
translations.idiomatic: Officials reported his conduct to the court, which commended him publicly.

sentences.zh: 何從義，延安洛川人。

translations.literal: He Congyi was a native of Luochuan in Yan'an.
translations.idiomatic: He Congyi came from Luochuan in Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 祖良、祖母李氏偕亡，從義廬於墓側，旦夕哀慕，不脫絰帶，不食菜果，惟啖疏食而已。

translations.literal: His grandfather Liang and grandmother, the Lady Li, died together; Congyi built a hut beside the grave, morning and evening mourned in longing, never removed his mourning sash, ate no vegetables or fruit, and consumed only coarse food.
translations.idiomatic: When his grandparents Liang and Lady Li died together, Congyi built a hut beside their grave, mourning day and night without removing his mourning sash, eating no vegetables or fruit—only plain coarse food.

sentences.zh: 事父世榮、母王氏，孝養尤至。

translations.literal: In serving his father Shirong and his mother, the Lady Wang, his filial support was especially thorough.
translations.idiomatic: He cared for his parents, Shirong and Lady Wang, with exceptional devotion.

sentences.zh: 伯祖溫、伯祖母郝氏，叔祖恭、叔祖母賀氏，叔祖讓、叔祖母姜氏，叔父珍、叔母光氏，皆無子。

translations.literal: His father's elder uncle Wen and elder aunt, the Lady Hao; his father's younger uncles Gong and Rang and their wives, the Ladies He and Jiang; and his father's younger brother Zhen and aunt, the Lady Guang—all were without sons.
translations.idiomatic: His great-uncle Wen and great-aunt Lady Hao, his uncles Gong and Rang and their wives Ladies He and Jiang, and his uncle Zhen and aunt Lady Guang—all were childless.

sentences.zh: 比其亡也，從義咸為治葬，築高墳，祭奠以禮，時人義之。

translations.literal: When each of them died, Congyi arranged burial for all, built high mounds, and performed sacrifices according to ritual—people of the time praised his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: When each died, Congyi arranged their burials, raised high mounds, and performed the rites properly—contemporaries honored his righteousness.

sentences.zh: 哈都赤，大都固安州人。

translations.literal: Qaduchi was a native of Gu'an Prefecture in the Great Capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Qaduchi came from Gu'an Prefecture in the capital region.

sentences.zh: 天性篤孝。

translations.literal: By nature he was deeply filial.
translations.idiomatic: He was deeply filial by nature.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，養母，母嘗有疾，醫治不痊，哈都赤礪其所佩小刀，拜天泣曰：「慈母生我劬勞，今當捐身報之。」

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he supported his mother; when his mother once fell ill and medical treatment did not cure her, Qaduchi sharpened the small knife he wore, bowed to Heaven and wept: "My loving mother bore me with toil; now I must give my body to repay her."
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he raised his mother alone; when she fell ill and doctors could not cure her, Qaduchi sharpened his knife, bowed to Heaven, and wept, "My mother bore me with endless labor—now I must give my flesh to repay her."

sentences.zh: 乃割開左脅，取肉一片，作羹進母，母曰：「此何肉也？

translations.literal: He then cut open his left side, took a piece of flesh, made it into broth and presented it to his mother; his mother said: "What meat is this?
translations.idiomatic: He cut open his left side, took a piece of flesh, cooked it into broth for her; his mother asked, "What meat is this?

sentences.zh: 其甘如是！」

translations.literal: How sweet it is!"
translations.idiomatic: How wonderfully sweet it is!"

sentences.zh: 數日而病癒。

translations.literal: Within several days her illness recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Within days she was cured.

sentences.zh: 高必達，建昌人。

translations.literal: Gao Bida was a native of Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Bida came from Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 五歲時，父明大忽棄家遠遊，莫知所適。

translations.literal: When he was five years old, his father Mingda suddenly abandoned the household and traveled far away; no one knew where he had gone.
translations.idiomatic: When he was five, his father Mingda suddenly left home on a long journey, and no one knew where he had gone.

sentences.zh: 必達既長，晝夜哀慕，乃娶妻以養母，而歷往四方求其父。

translations.literal: When Bida had grown up, day and night he mourned in longing; he took a wife to support his mother and traveled throughout the four directions seeking his father.
translations.idiomatic: When Bida grew up he grieved for his father day and night; he married to help support his mother and traveled everywhere in search of his father.

sentences.zh: 十餘年不得見，心愈悲。

translations.literal: For more than ten years he did not see him, and his heart grew ever more sorrowful.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten years passed without finding him, and his grief only deepened.

sentences.zh: 忽相傳黃州全真道院中有虛明子者，學道三十年矣，本姓高氏，建昌人也，匿姓名為道人云。

translations.literal: Suddenly it was reported that in the Quanzhen Daoist monastery at Huangzhou there was one called Master Xuming, who had studied the Way for thirty years; his original surname was Gao and he was from Jianchang, it was said, having concealed his name to become a Daoist.
translations.idiomatic: Word came that a Daoist called Master Xuming at the Quanzhen monastery in Huangzhou had studied the Way for thirty years; he was said to be a Gao from Jianchang who had hidden his identity.

sentences.zh: 必達詢問，知為父，即往拜之，具言家世，及己之所生歲月，大父母之喪葬始末，因哀號叩頭不已。

translations.literal: Bida made inquiries, learned it was his father, and at once went to pay respects; he recounted in full the family history, the month and year of his own birth, and the beginning and end of his grandparents' funerals, then wailed and knocked his head without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Bida investigated, learned it was his father, and went at once to bow before him; he told the whole family history, the date of his own birth, and every detail of his grandparents' burials, then wept and kowtowed without stopping.

sentences.zh: 虛明猶瞑坐不顧，久之，斥曰：「我非汝父，不去何為？」

translations.literal: Xuming still sat with eyes closed and paid no heed; after a long while he rebuked him: "I am not your father—why do you not leave?"
translations.idiomatic: Xuming kept his eyes closed and ignored him; at last he snapped, "I am not your father—why will you not go away?"

sentences.zh: 必達留侍左右不少懈，辭氣哀惻可矜。

translations.literal: Bida remained to attend at his side without the least slackening; his words and tone were mournful and pitiable.
translations.idiomatic: Bida stayed at his side without relenting, his words so sorrowful they moved all who heard.

sentences.zh: 其徒謂虛明曰：「師有子如此，忍弗歸乎？」

translations.literal: His disciples said to Xuming: "Master, with a son like this, can you bear not to return?"
translations.idiomatic: His disciples said to Xuming, "Master, with a son like this, how can you bear not to go home?"

sentences.zh: 虛明不得已，乃還家。

translations.literal: Xuming, having no choice, then returned home.
translations.idiomatic: At last Xuming yielded and went home.

sentences.zh: 必達孝養篤至，鄉里稱之。

translations.literal: Bida's filial support was deeply thorough, and the village praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Bida cared for his parents with devoted filial piety, and neighbors praised him.

sentences.zh: 曾德，漁陽人，宗聖公五十七代孫。

translations.literal: Zeng De was a native of Yuyang, fifty-seventh-generation descendant of the Duke of Zongsheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng De of Yuyang was the fifty-seventh-generation descendant of Confucius.

sentences.zh: 母早亡，父仲祥再娶左氏。

translations.literal: His mother died early; his father Zhongxiang remarried a Lady Zuo.
translations.idiomatic: His mother died young; his father Zhongxiang remarried a woman of the Zuo clan.

sentences.zh: 仲祥遊襄陽，樂其土俗，因攜左氏家焉。

translations.literal: Zhongxiang traveled to Xiangyang, delighted in its local customs, and therefore brought Lady Zuo's household to settle there.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxiang visited Xiangyang, took to the place, and moved there with Lady Zuo.

sentences.zh: 亂兵陷襄陽，遂失左氏。

translations.literal: Rebel troops overran Xiangyang, and Lady Zuo was lost.
translations.idiomatic: When rebel troops seized Xiangyang, Lady Zuo was lost.

sentences.zh: 德遍往南土求之，五年乃得於廣海間，奉迎以歸，孝養甚至。

translations.literal: De searched throughout the southern lands; after five years he found her in the Guanghai region, brought her home in welcome, and supported her with utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: De searched all through the south; after five years he found her near Guanghai, brought her home, and cared for her with devoted filial piety.

sentences.zh: 有司以聞，詔旌復其家。

translations.literal: The authorities reported upward; an imperial edict honored and restored his household.
translations.idiomatic: Officials reported his conduct to the throne, and an edict commended and restored his household.

sentences.zh: 靳昺，字克昌，絳州曲沃人。

translations.literal: Jin Biao, style name Kechang, was a native of Quwo in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Biao, styled Kechang, came from Quwo in Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 兄榮為奎章閣承製學士，奉母王氏官於朝。

translations.literal: His elder brother Rong was a Compiler Academician of the Kui Zhang Pavilion, supporting their mother, the Lady Wang, in office at court.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Rong served as Compiler Academician at the Kui Zhang Pavilion, bringing their mother Lady Wang with him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 母歿，昺與兄榮護喪還家。

translations.literal: When their mother died, Biao and his elder brother Rong escorted the coffin home.
translations.idiomatic: When their mother died, Biao and Rong escorted her coffin home.

sentences.zh: 至平定，大雷雨，流水驟至，昺伏柩上，榮呼之避水，昺不忍捨去，遂為水所漂沒。

translations.literal: When they reached Pingding, a great thunderstorm broke and floodwaters suddenly arrived; Biao lay upon the coffin, Rong called him to flee the water, but Biao could not bear to leave and was swept away and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: At Pingding a thunderstorm sent floodwaters rushing in; Biao clung to the coffin while Rong called him to flee, but Biao would not abandon his mother and was swept away and drowned.

sentences.zh: 後得王氏柩於三里外，得昺屍於五里外。

translations.literal: Later Lady Wang's coffin was found three li away, and Biao's corpse five li away.
translations.idiomatic: Later they found Lady Wang's coffin three li downstream and Biao's body five li away.

sentences.zh: 詔賜《孝子靳昺碑》。

translations.literal: An edict bestowed the 《Stele of the Filial Son Jin Biao》.
translations.idiomatic: The throne granted an inscribed stele titled 《The Filial Son Jin Biao》.

sentences.zh: 黃道賢，泉州人。

translations.literal: Huang Daoxian was a native of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Daoxian came from Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 嫡母唐無子，道賢在襁褓而生母蘇以疾去。

translations.literal: His principal mother, the Lady Tang, had no son; while Daoxian was still in swaddling clothes his birth mother, the Lady Su, left because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: His principal mother Lady Tang had no children of her own; while Daoxian was still an infant his birth mother Lady Su left home because of illness.

sentences.zh: 既長，思念生母，屢請於父，得召之歸。

translations.literal: When he had grown up, he longed for his birth mother and repeatedly asked his father, until she was summoned home.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up he yearned for his birth mother and begged his father again and again until she was brought home.

sentences.zh: 道賢竭力養二母，得其歡心。

translations.literal: Daoxian strove with all his strength to support both mothers and won their hearts' delight.
translations.idiomatic: Daoxian devoted himself to both mothers and won their affection.

sentences.zh: 父病篤，道賢晝夜奉湯藥，不離膝下，遍求良醫，莫效。

translations.literal: When his father fell gravely ill, Daoxian day and night presented broth and medicine, never leaving his knee; he sought good physicians everywhere, without effect.
translations.idiomatic: When his father fell gravely ill, Daoxian tended him day and night at his bedside and sought physicians everywhere, all to no avail.

sentences.zh: 乃夜禱於天，願減己一紀之算，以益父壽，其父遂愈。

translations.literal: He then prayed by night to Heaven, wishing to reduce his own allotted span by one cycle to add to his father's life—and his father then recovered.
translations.idiomatic: He prayed through the night to Heaven, offering twelve years of his own life for his father's—and his father recovered.

sentences.zh: 至元統二年乃歿，果符一紀之數。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiyuantong he died—indeed matching the count of one cycle.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Zhiyuantong—exactly twelve years later, as he had vowed.

sentences.zh: 道賢居喪盡禮，負土築墳，廬於墓側，疏食終制。

translations.literal: Daoxian observed mourning in full ritual, carried earth to build the mound, built a hut beside the grave, and ate only coarse food through the end of the mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: Daoxian observed every mourning rite, carried earth to raise the mound, lived in a hut beside the grave, and ate only plain food until mourning ended.

sentences.zh: 至元二年，有司上其事，旌其門曰「孝子黃氏之門」。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiyuan, the authorities reported the matter upward and honored his gate with the inscription "Gate of the Filial Son of the Huang Clan."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhiyuan, officials reported his conduct to the court, and his gate was honored with the plaque "Gate of the Filial Huang Family."

sentences.zh: 史彥斌，邳州人。

translations.literal: Shi Yanbin was a native of Pizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yanbin came from Pizhou.

sentences.zh: 嗜學，有孝行。

translations.literal: He loved learning and possessed conduct of filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and was known for filial conduct.

sentences.zh: 至正十四年，河溢，金鄉、魚台墳墓多壞。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhizheng the Yellow River overflowed, and many tombs in Jinxiang and Yutai were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Zhizheng the Yellow River flooded, destroying many graves in Jinxiang and Yutai.

sentences.zh: 彥斌母卒，慮有後患，乃為厚棺，刻銘曰「邳州沙河店史彥斌母柩」，仍以四鐵環釘其上，然後葬。

translations.literal: When Yanbin's mother died, fearing trouble later, he made a thick coffin and carved an inscription: "Coffin of the Mother of Shi Yanbin of Shahedian, Pizhou," and moreover nailed four iron rings upon it, then buried her.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, fearing future floods, Yanbin had a heavy coffin made, inscribed "Coffin of Shi Yanbin's mother, Shahedian, Pizhou," nailed four iron rings to it, and then buried her.

sentences.zh: 明年，墓果為水所漂，彥斌縛草為人，置水中，仰天呼曰：「母棺被水，不知其處，願天矜憐哀子之心，假此芻靈，指示母棺。」

translations.literal: The next year the grave was indeed swept away by water; Yanbin bound straw into a human figure, set it in the water, and cried to Heaven: "My mother's coffin has been carried off by water and I do not know where it is. May Heaven pity a grieving son's heart and lend this straw spirit to point out my mother's coffin."
translations.idiomatic: The next year the grave was swept away by floodwaters; Yanbin fashioned a straw figure, set it afloat, and cried to Heaven, "My mother's coffin has been carried off—I do not know where. Heaven, pity a son's grief and let this straw effigy lead me to her coffin."

sentences.zh: 言訖，涕泣橫流，乃乘舟隨草人所之。

translations.literal: When he had finished speaking, tears streamed across his face; he then took a boat and followed wherever the straw figure went.
translations.idiomatic: With tears streaming down his face, he took a boat and followed wherever the straw figure drifted.

sentences.zh: 經十餘日，行三百餘里，草人止桑林中，視之，母柩在焉，載歸复葬之。

translations.literal: After more than ten days and a journey of over three hundred li, the straw figure stopped in a mulberry grove; he looked and his mother's coffin was there—he carried it home and buried it again.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten days and three hundred li, the figure stopped in a mulberry grove; there he found his mother's coffin, brought it home, and buried her again.

sentences.zh: 張紹祖，字子讓，潁州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Shaozu, style name Zirang, was a native of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shaozu, styled Zirang, came from Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 讀書力學，以孝行聞於朝，特授河南路儒學教授。

translations.literal: He read books and studied diligently; his filial conduct became known at court, and he was specially appointed Professor of Confucian Learning on the Henan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: A diligent scholar, he won fame at court for filial piety and was specially appointed Professor of Confucian Learning on the Henan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 至正十五年，奉父避兵山間，賊至，執其父將殺之，紹祖泣曰：「吾父耆德善人，不當害，請殺我以代父死。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Zhizheng he brought his father to escape the troops in the mountains; bandits arrived, seized his father and were about to kill him. Shaozu wept and said: "My father is an aged man of virtue and goodness—he ought not be harmed. Please kill me in his place.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Zhizheng he took his father into the hills to escape the fighting; bandits seized his father to kill him. Shaozu wept, "My father is an old man of virtue—do not harm him. Kill me instead.

sentences.zh: 且若等非父母所生乎，何忍害人父也！」

translations.literal: Moreover, were you not born of parents yourselves—how can you bear to harm another man's father!"
translations.idiomatic: Were you not born of parents yourselves—how can you bear to kill another man's father!"

sentences.zh: 賊怒，以戈擊之，戈應手挫鈍，因感而相謂曰：「此真孝子，不可害。」

translations.literal: The bandits grew angry and struck him with a spear; the spear's point dulled in their hands. Moved, they said to one another: "This is a true filial son—we cannot harm him."
translations.idiomatic: The bandits struck him with a spear, but the blade dulled in their hands. Moved, they said to one another, "This is a true filial son—we cannot harm him.

sentences.zh: 乃釋之。

translations.literal: They then released them.
translations.idiomatic: They let them go.

sentences.zh: 李明德，瑞州路上高縣人。

translations.literal: Li Mingde was a native of Shanggao County on the Rui Prefecture Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mingde came from Shanggao County in Rui Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 讀書有志操，孝行篤至。

translations.literal: He read books and possessed firm resolve; his filial conduct was deeply thorough.
translations.idiomatic: A man of learning and firm principle, his filial devotion was profound.

sentences.zh: 至正十四年，亂兵陷袁州，因抄掠上高。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhizheng rebel troops overran Yuanzhou and consequently raided Shanggao.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Zhizheng rebel troops seized Yuanzhou and raided Shanggao.

sentences.zh: 兵執其父欲殺之，明德泣告曰：「子豈不能代父乎，願勿害吾父也！」

translations.literal: The soldiers seized his father intending to kill him; Mingde wept and pleaded: "Can a son not take his father's place? I beg you not to harm my father!"
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers seized his father to kill him; Mingde wept and pleaded, "Cannot a son die in his father's place? Please spare my father!

sentences.zh: 兵遂殺明德，而免其父，後以高壽終。

translations.literal: The soldiers then killed Mingde and spared his father, who later died at a great age.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers killed Mingde and spared his father, who lived to a ripe old age.

sentences.zh: 張緝，字士明，益都膠州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Ji, style name Shiming, was a native of Jiaozhou in Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji, styled Shiming, came from Jiaozhou in Yidu.

sentences.zh: 性孝友，能詩文。

translations.literal: By nature he was filial and brotherly, and able in poetry and prose.
translations.idiomatic: Filial and devoted to his brothers, he was also skilled in poetry and prose.

sentences.zh: 至正七年，與兄紳、弟經同領鄉薦，由澤州儒學正轉泰州幕職，棄之，養親居揚州。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhizheng he and his elder brother Shen and younger brother Jing together received provincial recommendation; from Rectifier of Confucian Learning in Ze Prefecture he was transferred to a staff post in Taizhou, which he abandoned to support his parents and live in Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Zhizheng he and his brothers Shen and Jing were all recommended for office; he left a post in Taizhou to care for his parents and settled in Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 十五年，揚州亂，緝母姬氏方臥病，賊突入臥內，舉槍欲刺姬，緝以身蔽姬，槍中緝脅，三日而死。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Yangzhou fell into disorder; Ji's mother, the Lady Ji, lay ill in bed when bandits burst into the sleeping chamber and raised a spear to stab her. Ji shielded Lady Ji with his body; the spear struck his ribs, and he died three days later.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, as Yangzhou fell into chaos, his mother Lady Ji lay ill when bandits burst in and raised a spear to kill her. Ji shielded her with his body; the spear pierced his side, and he died three days later.

sentences.zh: 魏敬益，字士友，雄州容城人。

translations.literal: Wei Jingyi, style name Shiyou, was a native of Rongcheng in Xiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jingyi, styled Shiyou, came from Rongcheng in Xiong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，居母喪，哀毀骨立。

translations.literal: By nature he was deeply filial; in mourning for his mother his grief and emaciation left him skin and bone.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply filial by nature, he wasted away to skin and bone mourning his mother.

sentences.zh: 素好施與​​，有男女失時者，出貲財為之嫁娶；

translations.literal: He had always loved giving; for men and women past marrying age he provided funds for their weddings;
translations.idiomatic: He was always generous; for men and women past marrying age he provided dowries and wedding expenses;

sentences.zh: 歲凶，老弱之飢者，為糜以食之。

translations.literal: in years of famine he made gruel for the hungry among the old and weak.
translations.idiomatic: and in famine years he cooked gruel for hungry old people and children.

sentences.zh: 敬益有田僅十六頃，一日語其子曰：「自吾買四莊村之田十頃，環其村之民皆不能自給，吾深憫焉。

translations.literal: Jingyi had only sixteen qing of fields; one day he said to his sons: "Since I bought the ten qing of fields at Sizhuang Village, the villagers all around cannot support themselves—I deeply pity them.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyi owned only sixteen qing of land; one day he told his sons, "Since I bought the ten qing at Sizhuang Village, the villagers there cannot support themselves, and I pity them deeply.

sentences.zh: 今將以田歸其人，汝謹守餘田，可無餒也。」

translations.literal: Now I shall return the fields to their people; you carefully keep the remaining fields and you need not go hungry."
translations.idiomatic: I am going to return that land to them; guard the rest carefully and you will not go hungry."

sentences.zh: 乃呼四莊村民諭之曰：「吾買若等業，使若等貧不聊生，有親無以養，吾之不仁甚​​矣，請以田歸若等。」

translations.literal: He then summoned the villagers of Sizhuang and told them: "I bought your livelihoods and made you so poor you cannot live—having parents yet unable to support them; my lack of benevolence is extreme. I ask to return the fields to you."
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the villagers and said, "I bought your land and left you unable to live or care for your parents—my cruelty was great. I return the fields to you."

sentences.zh: 眾聞，皆愕眙不敢受，強與之，乃受而言諸有司。

translations.literal: When all heard this they stared in astonishment and dared not accept; he pressed them until they accepted, and they then reported it to the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: The villagers were astonished and refused at first; he insisted until they accepted, and they reported his deed to the authorities.

sentences.zh: 有司以聞於中書，請加旌表。

translations.literal: The authorities reported upward to the Central Secretariat and requested additional public honor.
translations.idiomatic: Officials reported the matter to the Central Secretariat and requested that he be publicly commended.

sentences.zh: 丞相賀太平歎曰：「世乃有斯人哉！」

translations.literal: The Chancellor He Taiping sighed and said: "That the age should have such a man!"
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor He Taiping sighed, "That such a man should exist in our age!"

sentences.zh: 湯霖，字伯雨，龍興新建人。

translations.literal: Tang Lin, style name Boyu, was a native of Xinjian in Longxing.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Lin, styled Boyu, came from Xinjian in Longxing.

sentences.zh: 早喪父，事母至孝。

translations.literal: He lost his father early and served his mother with utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned of his father early, he was deeply filial toward his mother.

sentences.zh: 母嘗病熱，更數醫弗能效。

translations.literal: His mother once suffered from fever; several physicians in succession could not cure her.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell ill with fever, physician after physician failed to cure her.

sentences.zh: 母不肯飲藥，曰：「惟得冰，我疾乃可愈。」

translations.literal: His mother would not take medicine and said: "Only if I obtain ice can my illness be cured."
translations.idiomatic: She refused medicine and said, "Only ice can cure me."

sentences.zh: 爾時天氣甚燠，霖求冰不得，累日號哭於池上。

translations.literal: At that time the weather was very hot; Lin could not obtain ice and for many days wailed and wept beside the pond.
translations.idiomatic: The weather was sweltering; Lin could find no ice and wept for days beside a pond.

sentences.zh: 忽聞池中戛戛有聲，拭淚視之，乃冰澌也。

translations.literal: Suddenly he heard a crackling sound in the pond; wiping his tears he looked—it was ice floes.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly he heard crackling in the pond; wiping his tears he looked—ice had formed on the water.

sentences.zh: 亟取以奉母，其疾果愈。

translations.literal: He quickly took it and presented it to his mother, and her illness indeed recovered.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered it at once for his mother, and she recovered.

sentences.zh: 孫抑，字希武，世居晉寧洪洞縣。

translations.literal: Sun Yi, style name Xiwu, for generations dwelt in Hongtong County in Jinning.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yi, styled Xiwu, came from a family long settled in Hongtong County, Jinning.

sentences.zh: 抑登進士第，歷仕至刑部郎中。

translations.literal: Yi passed the jinshi examination and served in office up to Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Yi passed the jinshi examination and rose to Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 關保之變，挈父母妻子避兵平陽之柏村。

translations.literal: At the uprising of Guan Bao he took his parents, wife, and children to escape the troops to Baicun in Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Guan Bao rebelled, he fled with his parents, wife, and children to Baicun in Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 有亂兵至村剽掠，拔白刃嚇抑母，求財不得，舉刃欲斫之。

translations.literal: Rebel troops came to the village to plunder; drawing bare blades they frightened Yi's mother, and when they could not obtain wealth they raised their blades to hack her.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel soldiers raided the village; they threatened Yi's mother with drawn swords, and when she had no valuables to give, raised their blades to strike her down.

sentences.zh: 抑亟以身蔽母，請代受斫，母乃得釋。

translations.literal: Yi quickly shielded his mother with his body and asked to receive the blow in her place; his mother was then released.
translations.idiomatic: Yi threw himself before her and offered to take the blow; his mother was spared.

sentences.zh: 而抑父被虜去，不知所之。

translations.literal: But Yi's father was taken captive and no one knew where he had gone.
translations.idiomatic: His father, however, was taken captive, and no one knew where he had been taken.

sentences.zh: 或語之曰：「汝父被驅而東矣，然東軍得所掠民皆殺之，汝慎無往就死也。」

translations.literal: Someone told him: "Your father was driven eastward, but the eastern army kills all the people they capture—you must be careful not to go and court death."
translations.idiomatic: Someone warned him, "Your father was driven eastward, but the eastern army kills every captive they take—do not go to your death."

sentences.zh: 抑曰：「吾可畏死而棄吾父乎？」

translations.literal: Yi said: "Could I fear death and abandon my father?"
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "Could I fear death and abandon my father?

sentences.zh: 遂往，出入死地，屢瀕危殆，卒得父以歸。

translations.literal: He then went, passing in and out of deadly ground, repeatedly on the brink of peril, and in the end brought his father home.
translations.idiomatic: He went anyway, passing again and again through mortal danger, and at last brought his father home.

sentences.zh: 石永，紹興新昌人。

translations.literal: Shi Yong was a native of Xinchang in Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yong came from Xinchang in Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 性淳厚，事親至孝。

translations.literal: By nature he was sincere and honest, and in serving his parents he was deeply filial.
translations.idiomatic: Sincere and honest by nature, he was deeply filial toward his parents.

sentences.zh: 值亂兵掠鄉里，永父謙孫年八十，老不能行，永負父匿山谷中。

translations.literal: When rebel troops raided the countryside, Yong's father Qiansun was eighty years old and too aged to walk; Yong carried his father on his back and hid in a mountain valley.
translations.idiomatic: When rebel troops raided the countryside, Yong's father Qiansun was eighty and unable to walk; Yong carried him on his back into a mountain valley to hide.

sentences.zh: 亂兵執其父，欲殺之，永亟前抱父請以身代，兵遂殺永而釋其父。

translations.literal: The rebel troops seized his father intending to kill him; Yong quickly rushed forward, embraced his father, and asked to die in his place—the troops then killed Yong and released his father.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers seized his father to kill him; Yong rushed forward, embraced him, and begged to die in his place—the soldiers killed Yong and spared his father.

sentences.zh: 王克己，延安中部人。

translations.literal: Wang Keji was a native of Zhongbu in Yan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Keji came from Zhongbu in Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 父伯通歿，克己負土築墳，廬於墓側。

translations.literal: When his father Botong died, Keji carried earth to build the mound and built a hut beside the grave.
translations.idiomatic: When his father Botong died, Keji carried earth to raise the mound and lived in a hut beside the grave.

sentences.zh: 貊高縱兵暴掠，縣民皆逃竄，克己獨守墓不去。

translations.literal: Mo Gao let his troops plunder violently; the county people all fled, but Keji alone guarded the grave and would not leave.
translations.idiomatic: When Mo Gao's troops ravaged the county, everyone fled, but Keji alone stayed to guard the grave.

sentences.zh: 家人呼之避兵，克己曰：「吾誓守墓三年，以報吾親，雖死不可棄也。」

translations.literal: His family called him to flee the troops; Keji said: "I have sworn to guard the grave for three years to repay my parent—even death cannot make me abandon it."
translations.idiomatic: His family called him to flee; Keji said, "I swore to guard this grave for three years to repay my father—even death will not make me leave.

sentences.zh: 遂不去。

translations.literal: He then did not leave.
translations.idiomatic: He would not leave.

sentences.zh: 俄而兵至，見其身衣衰絰，形容憔悴，曰：「此孝子也！」

translations.literal: Before long the troops arrived; seeing him clothed in hemp mourning garb, his appearance haggard, they said: "This is a filial son!"
translations.idiomatic: Soon soldiers arrived; seeing him in mourning clothes, wasted and haggard, they said, "This is a filial son!"

sentences.zh: 遂不忍害，竟終喪而歸。

translations.literal: They then could not bear to harm him, and he completed the mourning period and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: They could not bear to harm him, and he completed his mourning and returned home.

sentences.zh: 劉思敬，延安宜君人。

translations.literal: Liu Sijing was a native of Yijun in Yan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Sijing came from Yijun in Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 事其繼母沙氏、杜氏，孝養之至，無異親母。

translations.literal: In serving his stepmothers, the Ladies Sha and Du, his filial support was thorough, no different from his birth mother.
translations.idiomatic: He cared for his stepmothers Lady Sha and Lady Du with the same devoted filial piety he would have shown a birth mother.

sentences.zh: 父年八十，兩目俱喪明，會亂兵剽掠其鄉，思敬負父避於巖穴中。

translations.literal: His father was eighty years old and both eyes had lost their sight; when rebel troops raided their village, Sijing carried his father on his back to hide in a rocky cave.
translations.idiomatic: His father was eighty and blind; when rebel troops raided their village, Sijing carried him on his back into a cave to hide.

sentences.zh: 有兵至，欲殺思敬，思敬泣言曰：「我父老矣，又無目，我死不足惜，使我父何依乎？」

translations.literal: Soldiers came intending to kill Sijing; Sijing wept and said: "My father is old and also without sight—my death is not worth regretting, but upon whom would my father rely?"
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers came to kill him; Sijing wept and said, "My father is old and blind—my death means nothing, but what would become of him?"

sentences.zh: 兵憐其孝，不忍殺，父子皆免於難。

translations.literal: The soldiers pitied his filial piety and could not bear to kill him; father and son both escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers pitied his filial piety and spared them both.

sentences.zh: 呂祐，字伯通，晉安人。

translations.literal: Lü You, style name Botong, was a native of Jin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Lü You, styled Botong, came from Jin'an.

sentences.zh: 至正二十六年，郡城破，有卒入其室，拔白刃脅其母林氏索財寶不得，揮刃欲斫母。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Zhizheng the prefectural city fell; a soldier entered his house, drew a bare blade and threatened his mother, the Lady Lin, demanding valuables; when he could not obtain them he swung his blade to hack at his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year of Zhizheng the prefectural city fell; a soldier entered their home, threatened his mother Lady Lin with a drawn sword for valuables, and when she had none, raised his blade to strike her.

sentences.zh: 祐急以身蔽母，而奪其刃，手指盡裂，被傷僕地。

translations.literal: You quickly shielded his mother with his body and seized the blade; his fingers were all torn apart, and wounded he fell to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: You threw himself before her and wrested away the blade, his fingers torn to shreds; wounded, he collapsed.

sentences.zh: 良久而蘇，開目視母曰：「母幸無恙，我死無憾矣。」

translations.literal: After a long while he revived, opened his eyes, looked at his mother and said: "Mother, fortunately you are unharmed—I die without regret."
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he revived, looked at his mother, and said, "Mother, you are safe—I can die without regret.

sentences.zh: 遂瞑目死。

translations.literal: He then closed his eyes and died.
translations.idiomatic: He closed his eyes and died.

sentences.zh: 周樂，溫州瑞安人。

translations.literal: Zhou Le was a native of Ruian in Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Le came from Ruian in Wen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宋狀元坦之後，父日成，通經能文。

translations.literal: A descendant of the Song dynasty zhuangyuan Tan, his father Richeng was versed in the classics and able in writing.
translations.idiomatic: A descendant of the Song zhuangyuan Tan, his father Richeng was a classical scholar and accomplished writer.

sentences.zh: 海賊竊據溫州，拘日成置海舟上，樂隨往，事其父甚謹。

translations.literal: Sea bandits seized Wenzhou, detained Richeng and placed him on a seagoing vessel; Le followed along and served his father with great care.
translations.idiomatic: Sea pirates seized Wenzhou, took Richeng aboard a ship, and Le went with him, tending his father with scrupulous care.

sentences.zh: 一日賊酋遣人沉日成於水，樂泣請曰：「我有祖母，幸留父侍養，請以己代父死。」

translations.literal: One day the bandit chief sent men to sink Richeng in the water; Le wept and pleaded: "I have a grandmother—please spare my father to support her; I ask to die in my father's place."
translations.idiomatic: One day the pirate chief ordered Richeng thrown into the sea; Le wept and pleaded, "I have a grandmother who needs my father—let me die in his place."

sentences.zh: 不聽，樂抱父不忍舍，遂同死焉。

translations.literal: They would not listen; Le embraced his father and could not bear to let go, and so they died together.
translations.idiomatic: They refused; Le clung to his father and would not let go, and both drowned together.
